title: Pseudotyping lentiviral particles with SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein for neutralization assays
author: Katharine H. D. Crawford
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.br44m8yw

To determine viral titers, use either flow cytometry (for viruses packaging the ZsGreen backbone) or a luciferase assay (for viruses packaging the Luciferase-IRES-ZsGreen backbone). Coat a 96-well cell-culture plate with 25 µL, poly-L-lysine per well according to manufacturer's protocol (Millipore Sigma, P4707). steps.title: Seed 293T Cells
steps.instruction: Seed 293T cells in D10 Growth Media in a 6-well plate at 5x10^5 cells per well (2.5x10^5 cells per mL) to achieve 50-70% confluency the next day.

steps.title: Transfect Cells for Viral Production
steps.instruction: At 16-24 hours after seeding, transfect cells using BioT according to manufacturer's instructions with the following plasmid mix per well of a 6-well plate:

substeps.instruction: 1 µg lentiviral backbone (ZsGreen or Luciferase-IRES-ZsGreen)
0.22 µg plasmid HMD-Hgpm2
0.22 µg plasmid pRC-CMV-Rev1b
0.22 µg plasmid HDM-tat1b
0.34 µg viral entry protein: SARS-CoV-2 Spike (NR-52513, NR-52514, NR-52515, NR-53742, or NR-53765), VSV G (positive control), or transfection carrier DNA (Promega E4881) as a negative control
Note: Spike plasmid NR-53765 (BEI) or 158762 (AddGene) with 21 amino acid cytoplasmic tail deletion and D614G mutation is recommended

steps.title: Media Change and Virus Collection
steps.instruction: Maintain and harvest the pseudotyped lentiviral particles.

substeps.instruction: Change media to fresh, pre-warmed D10 at 18 to 24 hours post-transfection
At 60 hours post-transfection, collect virus by harvesting the supernatant
Filter supernatant through a 0.45 um SFCA low protein-binding filter
Store virus at 4 °C for immediate use or freeze at -80 °C

steps.title: Seed 293T-ACE2 Cells for Titering
steps.instruction: Seed a poly-L-lysine-coated 96-well plate with 1.25x10^4 293T-ACE2 cells (BEI NR-52511) per well in D10 media (50 µL per well at 2.5x10^5 cells/mL).

substeps.instruction: Use black-walled, clear-bottom, poly-L-lysine coated plates (e.g., Greiner Bio-One 655936) for luciferase readout
Examine cells 12-24 hours post-seeding; they should be ~15-20% confluent
If titering via flow cytometry, count at least 2 wells to determine cell number at infection

steps.title: Prepare Viral Serial Dilutions
steps.instruction: Prepare serial dilutions of viruses in D10 growth media for a final infection volume of 150 µL (100 µL virus added to 50 µL media already in wells).

substeps.instruction: ZsGreen virus: start with 1:3 dilution, then 4 serial 1:5 dilutions
Spike-pseudotyped Luciferase_IRES_ZsGreen: start with 1:5 or 1:10 dilution, then 5 serial 1:2 to 1:3 dilutions
VSV G-pseudotyped Luciferase_IRES_ZsGreen: start with 1:50 dilution
Include 'bald' virus particles (no entry protein) as a negative control

steps.title: Infect Cells and Determine Titer
steps.instruction: Infect cells and analyze via flow cytometry to calculate titers.

substeps.instruction: Slowly add 100 µL of virus dilutions to the 50 µL of D10 media in the wells
Identify wells that appear ~1-10% positive under a fluorescent microscope
Harvest cells from selected wells using trypsin and transfer to V-bottom plates or microcentrifuge tubes
Pellet cells at 300xg for 4 min
Wash twice with 3% BSA in PBS
Resuspend in 1% BSA in PBS and analyze via flow cytometry (e.g., BD Celesta, 530/30 filter, FITC channel; analyze with FlowJo v10)
Calculate titer per mL using Poisson formula: -ln(1 – P / 100) x (number of cells / well) / (volume of virus per well in mL), where P is percentage of ZsGreen positive cells

steps.title: Seed Cells for Neutralization Assay
steps.instruction: Seed a poly-L-lysine-coated 96-well plate with 1.25x10^4 293T-ACE2 cells (BEI NR-52511) per well in 50 µL DMEM (2.5x10^5 cells per mL).

substeps.instruction: Use black-walled, clear bottom plates for luciferase readout
Plan to infect 8–20 hours post-seeding

steps.title: Prepare Serum and Virus Setup Plate
steps.instruction: Prepare a separate 96-well 'setup' plate for serum and virus dilutions approximately 1.5 hours before infection.

substeps.instruction: Serially dilute serum samples, leaving 60 µL diluted serum per well
Add 60 µL D10 to 'virus only' and 'virus plus cells' control wells
Add 120 µL D10 to 'media only' and 'cells only' control wells
Dilute virus to ~2-4x10^6 RLU per mL and add 60 µL to all serum dilution wells and virus control wells (target: 200,000-800,000 RLUs for wells without serum)
Incubate the virus and serum mixture at 37 °C for 1 hour

steps.title: Infect Cells and Incubate
steps.instruction: Transfer the virus-serum mixture to the cells and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Carefully add 100 µL from each well of the setup plate to the corresponding wells of the 293T-ACE2 cell plate
Incubate at 37 °C for 48 to 72 hours (or 48 to 60 hours as per alternative section) until cells are completely confluent but not overgrown

steps.title: Luciferase Readout and Data Analysis
steps.instruction: Measure luminescence using the Bright-Glo Luciferase Assay System (Promega, E2610).

substeps.instruction: Thaw luciferase reagent at room temperature
Remove 100 µL media from each well, leaving ~30 µL
Add 30 µL luciferase reagent, mix well (avoid bubbles), and transfer the 60 µL to a black-bottom plate (e.g., Costar 07-200-590) if not already using a black-walled clear-bottom plate
Incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature in the dark
Measure luminescence using a plate reader (e.g., Tecan Infinite M1000 Pro, no attenuation, 1s integration time)
Subtract background signal (average of 'virus only' and 'virus + 293Ts' wells)
Calculate 'fraction infectivity' by dividing the RLU of each experimental well by the average of the two 'virus + cells' positive control wells in the same row/column
Plot data using neutcurve Python package (three-parameter Hill curve)

description: Plot the data. First, subtract the average of the background (virus only and virus+293Ts (if included)) wells from all wells. Then, calculate the fraction infectivity for each experimental well (containing plasma or antibody) compared to the virus plus cells positive control wells. We do this by dividing the RLU reading for the experimental well by the average of the RLU readings for the two virus plus cells positive control wells in the same row or column as the experimental well. This protocol used the Neutcurve Python package to plot the data.
